skill.name: landing-page-design
skill.description: Guides AI agents through conversion-focused landing page design, including hero sections, CTA copy, social proof, forms, mobile layout, and page speed.
skill.summary: Design conversion-focused landing pages with practical layout, copy, CTA, social proof, mobile, and speed guidance.
skill.author: halt-catch-fire

security_audit.summary: The skill is primarily design guidance, but it includes several explicit examples that run belt and npx commands. Those commands appear aligned with image generation, search, and skill setup, with no evidence of prompt injection or hidden malicious intent.

remediation.issue: The skill asks users to run external CLI and installation commands.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear consent note before each command group and explain which provider receives data.

remediation.issue: Some examples send prompts, research questions, or HTML to external services.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to include secrets, private customer data, or unreleased product details in these inputs.

remediation.issue: The CLI installation instructions rely on a hardcoded raw GitHub URL.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a stable documentation page with integrity and publisher information for installation steps.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 7 instructs users to run an npx-based skill installation command. This is intentional setup guidance, but it still asks users to execute external package tooling.
Line 15 only names the belt CLI inside Markdown backticks. The executable installation concern is covered separately by the hardcoded external URL finding.
Lines 17-31 contain bash examples for belt login, image generation, and web search. These commands run an external CLI and send prompts or queries to network services.
Lines 31-38 are Markdown fence and explanatory layout text. They do not contain executable shell commands or dynamic code execution.
Lines 38-52 are an ASCII layout diagram in a Markdown code fence. The backticks are formatting, not shell or Ruby execution.
Lines 52-78 contain Markdown formatting, tables, and headline guidance. No executable command appears in this span.
Lines 78-87 are example headline text inside a Markdown code fence. They are design examples, not command execution.
Lines 87-93 close a text example and introduce hero image guidance. The span contains no shell command or executable code.
Lines 93-101 are hero image examples in Markdown formatting. The content is prose guidance, not an external command.
Lines 101-103 only close and open Markdown fences. The actual belt commands begin later and are adjudicated in the line 103 finding.
Lines 103-116 include belt app run commands for third-party image models. The examples send prompt text to external model providers through the CLI.
Lines 116-169 contain landing page design tables and prose. No executable shell command is present in this span.
Lines 169-174 include a belt app run command for an external answer service. It may transmit the research question to a network-backed provider.
Lines 174-201 contain form, mobile, and page guidance plus a Markdown fence marker. No command is executed in this span.
Lines 201-213 contain belt app run commands for image generation and HTML-to-image conversion. These commands may send prompts and HTML content to external services.
Lines 213-240 contain page speed guidance, common mistakes, and a Markdown fence marker. The executable related-skill commands are covered by the line 240 finding.
Lines 240-244 list npx skills add commands for installing additional skills. This asks users to execute external installation commands from a remote package ecosystem.
Lines 244-246 include an inline belt app store command. It is a low-context external CLI action, though it appears to list available apps rather than run a payload.
Line 11 explicitly depends on inference.sh for AI-generated visuals. This is legitimate for the skill, but it establishes a third-party network dependency.
Line 15 links to raw GitHub install instructions for the required CLI. The URL is transparent, but it encourages fetching external setup guidance.
Line 106 is an image prompt describing positive growth charts in a marketing scene. It does not request system discovery, host enumeration, or reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Teams often ship landing pages with weak headlines, unclear CTAs, and poor mobile flow. This skill gives practical design rules for pages that communicate value quickly and support conversion.
actual_capabilities: Defines an above-the-fold structure with headline, subheadline, CTA, hero image, and social proof.
Provides headline formulas and examples for clearer product value statements.
Gives CTA copy and layout rules for stronger conversion paths.
Recommends section order for SaaS, startup, and product landing pages.
Includes mobile, form, page speed, and OG image guidance.
Shows optional belt commands for image generation and landing page research.
limitations: It provides guidance, not a complete landing page implementation.
Conversion advice is general and still needs user testing.
External image and search examples require the belt CLI and provider access.
It does not replace brand strategy, legal review, or accessibility testing.

use_cases.title: Improve a Startup Homepage
use_cases.description: Refine the hero section, CTA wording, trust signals, and section order for a new product launch.

use_cases.title: Audit SaaS Conversion Flow
use_cases.description: Check whether a SaaS page explains value quickly, supports trust, and repeats the primary action clearly.

use_cases.title: Guide AI Page Generation
use_cases.description: Give Claude, Codex, or Claude Code concrete landing page rules before generating copy, layout, or image prompts.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Landing Page Outline
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when starting a new product landing page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the landing-page-design skill to outline a landing page for [product]. Include the hero, CTA, social proof, features, pricing, FAQ, and final CTA.

prompt_templates.title: Improve My Hero Section
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a page has weak above-the-fold messaging.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this hero section with the landing-page-design skill: [paste copy]. Rewrite the headline, subheadline, CTA, and social proof line.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Mobile Landing Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when mobile conversion matters most.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the landing-page-design skill to create a mobile-first structure for [audience]. Include tap targets, sticky CTA behavior, forms, and image guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Conversion Design Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when reviewing an existing SaaS or product page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this landing page using the landing-page-design skill: [paste page content]. Identify conversion blockers, missing proof, CTA problems, and prioritized fixes.

output_examples.input: A founder asks for an above-the-fold structure for a developer documentation product.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a concise hero plan with an outcome-focused headline, explanatory subheadline, primary CTA, proof line, and outcome-based image direction.

output_examples.input: A marketer asks why a SaaS landing page is not converting.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies vague copy, weak CTA text, missing proof, too many form fields, and mobile layout risks, then suggests practical fixes.

output_examples.input: A designer asks for hero image ideas for a productivity tool.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests outcome-focused scenes, before-and-after visuals, and product-in-context directions that support the page message.

best_practices: Start with the customer outcome before choosing layout, images, or CTA text.
Use one primary CTA and repeat it after major sections.
Review mobile layout, form length, image weight, and page speed before launch.
anti_patterns: Do not lead with vague claims such as welcome messages or broad AI buzzwords.
Do not use decorative hero images that fail to show the product outcome.
Do not ask users to run external commands with private data in prompts or HTML.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps plan and improve conversion-focused landing pages for products, startups, and SaaS offers.

faq.question: Can it generate a complete website?
faq.answer: It gives design and content guidance. An AI coding agent still needs to build the final page.

faq.question: Does it support image generation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes optional belt CLI examples for hero images and OG images through external providers.

faq.question: Is it useful without the belt CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. The layout, copy, CTA, social proof, mobile, and speed guidance works without external tools.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Founders, marketers, designers, and developers can use it to improve product landing pages.

faq.question: What should users avoid sharing?
faq.answer: Users should avoid sending secrets, private customer data, or unreleased product details to external services.
